q1.answer: ADR013 (use node-fetch) is superseded by ADR014 and no longer in force. ADR014 says all Node.js code should use native fetch, while frontend plugins/packages like this one should keep using the fetchApiRef abstraction (injected via useApi), which is exactly why NotificationsClient takes fetchApi in its constructor instead of importing an HTTP library.

q2.answer: ADR007 requires using MSW (setupServer/http.get handlers) to mock any fetch or XMLHTTPRequest traffic in all tests. It says this avoids each test having its own ad-hoc implementation of mocking network requests, i.e. it standardizes the approach repo-wide (compared to mocking fetch/fetchApi directly per test).

q3.answer: ADR006 cites that React.FC implicitly added a children prop to every component, and that it did not support a generic type on children. It notes Facebook removed React.FC from the create-react-app TypeScript template because it was found to be an unnecessary feature with next to no benefit alongside those downsides.

q4.answer: ADR010 names Moment.js as the library luxon replaces, giving two reasons: Moment.js suffers from large bundle sizes and mutable state issues, and separately Moment.js itself is being sunset/deprecated with its own project recommending alternatives.

q5.answer: ADR004 requires every exported symbol to be traceable through index files all the way to the package's root src/index.ts. It was written specifically to make it easy to answer 'is this export in this module also exported by the package?' / 'what is exported from this directory?'.

q6.answer: No: under ADR004's rule, a symbol is only part of the public API if it can be traced through an unbroken chain of re-exporting index files up to src/index.ts. Since there is no src/utils/index.ts and src/index.ts never mentions notificationLinks.ts or plainText.ts, that chain is broken, so per the rule these files are not exported/public even though nothing explicitly marks them private — the absence of a re-export path itself makes them internal.

q7.answer: ADR011 says an x-react package is for shared widgets, hooks, and similar code that both the plugin itself (x) and third-party frontend plugins can depend on. For notifications to need a notifications-react package, there would have to be components/hooks in this plugin that other, third-party frontend plugins want to reuse/depend on (not just internal use within the notifications plugin itself).

q8.answer: ADR003 allows a default export only when 'absolutely necessary,' citing React.lazy modules as that one exception (since React.lazy's dynamic import expects a default export). For teams wanting to avoid even that, it gives the workaround of mapping the named export to a default inside the .then() of the dynamic import, e.g. `React.lazy(() => import('../path/to/Component').then(m => ({ default: m.Component })))`.

q9.answer: ADR015 defines the loader/component option pattern for JSX elements and components. Its Consequences section says they will update all APIs for the new frontend system (@backstage/frontend-* packages) but will NOT update any existing APIs for the old frontend system (@backstage/core-* packages) — meaning pre-existing dev-app-style code like this one is not meant to be retrofitted.
